cohort: The study involved 670 women who had either a vaginal birth of a fetus in breech presentation (224 women) or cephalic presentation (446 women), matched for birthweight, date of delivery, and vaginal parity.
finding: There was no statistically significant difference in the incidence of obstetric anal sphincter injuries between women who had a breech vaginal birth compared to cephalic vaginal birth.
mod_finding: The incidence of obstetric anal sphincter injuries did not significantly differ between breech and cephalic vaginal births (0.9% vs. 1.1%).
